title: Social differences in children's health in Hungary in the 2010s
title_hu: Társadalmi különbségek a gyermekek egészségi állapotában Magyarországon a 21. század második évtizedében
summary_en: How unequal is children's health by family income in Hungary? Hajdú and Kertesi document the social gradient in child-health outcomes — birth weight, hospitalisation, chronic-condition prevalence — across Hungarian families in the 2010s using linked administrative health and tax data. They find substantial gaps along the income gradient that are similar in magnitude to those documented for the US and Western Europe, and trace the gaps to early-life conditions rather than later behavioural choices alone.
policy_relevance: Direct policy relevance for Hungarian child-poverty and public-health programmes (EMMI Gyermek-egészségügyi stratégia, Belügyminisztérium child-protection): the early-life evidence supports prioritising prenatal-care and early-childhood interventions over later remedial programmes. Useful for the calibration of EU Child Guarantee Hungarian Action Plan.
